newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to allow Chinese fishing vessels to pass.
newsitem.headline: Manila to allow Chinese fishing vessels to pass.

text.p: The Philippines is allowing Chinese vessels to pass through its territory on their way to fishing grounds in international waters in the Pacific, President Fidel Ramos said on Tuesday.
Speaking at a news conference in Iligan city on southern Mindanao island, Ramos said he hoped China would make a reciprocal gesture.

The two countries have clashed diplomatically recently over the ownership of some islands in the South China Sea, particularly in the Spratlys, a cluster of potentially oil-rich isles, reefs and shoals.
Beijing claims ownership of all the islands in the South China sea. The Spratlys are also claimed wholly or in part by Vietnam, Taiwan, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
"This is one way of our cooperating with our neighbouring country. This is for mutual benefit," Ramos told the news conference, broadcast on a government radio station.
"We do them a favour now, maybe they'll do you a favour next time," he added.

"As long as the intention is peaceful, it is announced well ahead and there is a processing of our government agencies to verify and an open disclosure of intentions of the foreign missions, then there is no problem," Ramos said.
Last month the Philippines accused China of sending warships near areas claimed by Manila in the Spratlys. Beijing said the ships were research vessels on a scientific mission.
